ThreadRole.description:
Who said it.

``founder`` and ``composer`` only. There is no ``system`` role: a thread is the record of a
conversation a person had, and anything the studio injected into the model's context is not part
of that conversation. Recording it here would put words in a founder's history they never saw.
ThreadRole.title: ThreadRole

text.description:
What was said, verbatim. Never summarised — the thread is cited as the source of a
revision, and a summary cannot be a source.
text.title: Text

description:
A founder's conversation about one ticket (fountainbridge FB-126, gap G4).

Every ticket in the desk design carries "Discuss in the composer". A founder reads what their team
proposes, disagrees with one line, says so in their own words, and the change files as a revision
the lane picks up. That only works if the conversation outlives the browser tab — transcripts lived
in ``localStorage`` until this (FB-065, deliberately), so the reasoning behind a revision was gone
the moment the tab closed and the trail could never answer *why* a ticket changed.

Lives on the venture repo's ``foundry-state`` ref under ``threads/``, beside ``approvals/``,
``prps/`` and ``runreports/`` — machine-written venture state the studio and the lanes both read.
Not ``context/``: that is reviewed content behind a pull request, and a pull request per message is
not a conversation.

repo.description:
The venture repository the ticket lives in. Two repos in one venture may share an id
namespace, so a thread is only identified by both.
repo.title: Repo

ticket_id.description: The ticket this conversation is about, e.g. ``ARCA-068``.
ticket_id.title: Ticket Id
